architecture.mechanism: Pressure gradient engineering using Darcy's law to drive fluid flow through a resistive medium by applying a controlled vacuum
architecture.intervention: Integrate a localized vacuum-assist chamber or pressure gradient control element at the proximal end of the multi-lumen tubing to establish a controlled negative pressure differential, reducing the internal positive driving pressure required to maintain target flow rates while preserving the existing wall thickness and geometry needed for kink resistance and lumen patency
architecture.expected_effect: Reduced effective pressure loss across the tubing length by supplementing the driving force with a distal-to-proximal pressure gradient, maintaining full lumen patency and kink resistance without altering the mechanical cross-section of the tubing
architecture.falsification_test: Measure the pressure drop across a standardized length of multi-lumen tubing at a fixed flow rate with and without the applied proximal vacuum gradient; if the pressure drop does not decrease by at least 15% while passing a standard kink-resistance mandrel test and maintaining minimum lumen diameter under bending, the intervention fails
